questions.q: What does the integer that MLflow assigns to a new model version (1, 2, 3...) actually tell you about the model's content?
options: Nothing by itself — it's a stable identity, not a description of what's inside
It encodes the accuracy of the model
It encodes the exact training date and time
It encodes the semantic version (major.minor.patch) automatically
questions.explain: The version number is just an auto-incrementing, collision-free identity. Everything meaningful about the content has to be attached separately, as tags.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four things that should travel with a model version to make it reproducible?
options: The exact code version (git commit)
The exact data version (snapshot or hash)
Every hyperparameter used in training
The name of the engineer who clicked "train"
questions.explain: Reproducibility depends on code version, data version, hyperparameters, and environment — not on who happened to run the job.

questions.q: Why is a model version tag preferable to a note in Slack or a notebook comment for recording something like a dataset snapshot ID?
options: Tags load faster than Slack messages
A tag is structured and queryable (e.g. via search_model_versions), while a chat message or comment is not
Slack does not allow text longer than 280 characters
Notebooks cannot store strings
questions.explain: A tag can be searched programmatically across every version in the registry, which is exactly what's needed when, for example, a bad dataset snapshot needs to be traced to every affected model.

questions.q: Why does this lesson distinguish a model version's number from an alias like "champion"?
options: They are actually the same thing in MLflow
The version number is immutable identity (what the model is); the alias is a mutable role (what it's currently doing) — conflating them was the flaw in the old stage field
Aliases can only be used on archived versions
Version numbers are deprecated in favor of aliases
questions.explain: Keeping identity (version) and role (alias) separate avoids the structural problem that made the old single stage field brittle.

questions.q: A team wants to express "this was a major architecture change" vs. "this was a routine retrain" without fighting MLflow's integer versioning. What's the recommended approach?
options: Rename the version number to a semantic string like v2.1.0
Add a tag such as release_type with value "major" or "minor"
Delete and re-register the model under a new name each time
Use the deprecated stage field to represent this distinction
questions.explain: Since the registry version is always a plain integer, teams add the semantic meaning they want as a separate tag rather than trying to override the registry's own numbering.
